en: Huh, I had no idea.
Whaddya do when it comes to datin' guys?
Hmm? What do you mean?
What places do ya like goin' to on dates?
Let me think... I like going to the movies.
Movies? That's pretty typical.
They've got 3D movies now, you know? Where you have to wear glasses. I can wear those and then nobody can tell if I fall asleep.
If it's a movie I've already seen I know what happens, so I can still talk about it after it's over. That's my routine when I go out with clients.
If ya don't wanna go out, then just say so...
What's it like when ya fall for a guy? Do ya tell them ya like 'em?
Yeah, I go on the offensive pretty fast.
I see. Yer more forward than I woulda expected.
Well that way, if he's into me, I've caught a lucky break. And if he's not, then I find out right away and can move on to my next love.
Ya make it sound so simple. Ya don't get shaken up from bein' rejected?
If I tell a guy when I first feel like I'm interested, it's not big deal if he turns me down. It's better than pining after him forever.
Heh. Yer a real no-nonsense gal, aren't ya?
How old do ya like yer guys?
Oh, I am waaay into older guys!
Really now? How come?
How come? Because younger guys don't really feel like men to me. They're kind of childish, I think.
Older guys are better looking and more distinguished, too. They're way more reliable!
A man's gotta be reliable. Ones who use a woman to support 'em are no good in my book.
I hear you there! I can't stand guys who don't have jobs. But I'm guessing that's not an issue with you, Saejima-san.
Uh, well, I am kinda takin' a break from work right now...
What!? Really? Shouldn't you be off at a job somewhere instead of hanging out at a club like this?
Yer the last person I wanna hear that from...
Would ya date an old guy then?
Not if he's some decrepit old grandpa, but if he's in good shape, then I'd be okay with that.
Really? Even if he's baldin' and stuff?
That's super sexy, though. I'm really into that look some foreigners have, with shaved heads and beards.
Guess bein' bald has its perks.
Mind if I ask ya somethin' about yerself?
Do ya got any special talents?
Special talents? Hmm...
Oh! I'm good at walking.
What? How do ya mean?
You know how in fashion shows the models need to walk with a sexy sort of shimmy to their shoulders and hips?
Oh, okay. I think I get what ya mean.
Sometimes when I'm out walking I'll do that, and get some guys to turn their heads! It's super, super fun!
I guess that's sort of a special talent.
Do ya got any siblings?
I have a younger sister.
Hey, same as me.
Oh, so you're the big brother, huh?
And yer the big sister.
Well, my younger sister is already married and has kids.
Really? She moves pretty fast.
Yeah. Thanks to her, I've already wound up as an aunt at my age.
Nothin' wrong with that.
But we're nothin' alike. My sister really had it together.
Same with me! My sister up and married her boss and has kids now. And I'm here without even a full time job.
You and me are like two peas in a pod, huh?
Ha! Seems so.
Say that again.
Uh... So you're the big brother, Saejima-san?
Big brother, huh... Ngh...
Saejima-san, is something the matter? Did... Did I say something wrong?
No, it's fine. Just... been a while since anyone called me that.
Is Kaguya yer real name?
Of course not. It's just my work name.
Why'd ya go with Kaguya then?
Well, we're in Tsukimino. "Tsuki" is moon, and Kaguya was the Moon Princess.
Everyone picks their hostess name like that. Some girls even take names from male idol singers they're fans of, like Ryo or Akira.
Yeah, I guess those could be girls' names, too.
In Tokyo they take on surnames, too. They make sure not to use kanji that are too complicated, so that it looks cute.
So I've been wonderin' somethin'.
What are yer measurements?
Lemme think... 94, 58, 87 from top to bottom. And I'm a G-cup.
I dunno what any of that means...
Hehe. When other customers hear G-cup, their eyes go right to my breasts! But you're more innocent than that, Saejima-san!
Uh, I see.
Do ya want kids?
Getting married and giving birth sound like a huge pain. But I suppose it'd be fun to have kids around if I did.
Would ya want a boy or a girl?
Hmm. I guess I'd prefer a boy.
Me too. I'd like to get a shot at raisin' a son tough enough to take me on.
I bet you'd be a passionate teacher. I'm way more hands-off. I'd be all, hey, do whatever you want.
That's okay, too. I guess ya could say I sorta raised myself.
Hmm. I guess that could be a good way to raise a kid, too.
Yeah. Maybe it's good fer a boy to be pushed out into the harshness of reality.
Because I feel a boy would be better at making money in the future!
A girl would probably wind up becoming a lazy bum like me.
Ya sure got a knack for thinkin' up useless situations.
How 'bout adoption? Then ya wouldn't hafta get married.
I don't know. Can an unmarried part-timer like me even adopt a child? I can barely afford to support my own lifestyle.
That's true. My sister and I were taken in by our relatives, and havin' two extra kids was a mighty big expense for 'em.
I guess being broke means I can't have kids then.
It'd be hard, yeah.
Which are ya? A dom or a sub?
Huh!? I've never thought about it.
Hmm... I guess a sub?
I wouldn't of guessed.
For me, I'd rather go with the flow than have to do anything myself. So I let the guy call the shots.
I don't have any real urge to figure out whether to do this or that to someone else.
I think that's just bein' lazy...

Hello there. Welcome to La Seine.
Our establishment has an 8,400 yen minimum, along with a 3,150 yen cover charge. Choosing a specific hostess incurs another 3,150 yen fee.
You'd like to see Riku-san? This way, sir.
I'm terribly sorry, sir, but Riku-san isn't available at the moment, I'm afraid.
I see. I'll come back later, then.
Hold on!
Sorry. I'll have to come back later.
(I'll need at least 15,000 yen.)
(I can't afford an extension right now.)
No thanks. I'll be on my way.
(Should I change the subject?)
(Maybe I should ask a question?)
(Maybe I should order something?)
(I should be on my way.)
(She already said yes. I shouldn't be so pushy about it.)
(She already turned me down once. I should probably wait before I ask her again.)
You're not from around here, are ya, Kiryu-san?
Not originally. I've lived here for six months now, though. Is it that obvious?
Kinda, yeah. You've got a Tokyo accent. It's easy to tell if someone's not from 'round here.
I don't think you have a thick accent.
Yeah, folks come here from all over, so I try to tone it down. Non-locals probably wouldn't be able to understand me otherwise.
Let me hear it. Just a little bit.
Ehhh, I dunno if that's a good idea, Kiryu-san. I don't think you're gonna understand me.
Try me. Just let yourself speak like you normally would.
You're right. Still, I think it's nice when a girl speaks with an accent.
Oh? Y'like girls with an accent, Kiryu-san?
I've certainly got nothing against them.
Probably not, no. Sometimes I have trouble understanding what locals are trying to say when I talk to them.
Older folks have an even thicker accent! Heck, sometimes people my age have a tough time figurin' out what they're trying to say.
What does it sound like?
Hmm, let's see... Hey wait, you're just tryin' to make me speak!
Oh geez, right when I've lowered my guard...
Jes' don't 'spect me t'learn ya howta unnerstannit when ya up n' ask me outta the blue like this 'un.
Sumthin' th' matter? Y'look like yer jaw done hit th' floor.
I'm jes' talkin' th' way y'done askin' me to, Kiryu-san, is all.
Huh? Sure what?
Did y'get all that?
Uh, yeah, of course.
Uh-huh. Sure ya did. I'll keep my accent in check around ya, Kiryu-san.
Please speak normally. You were right. I didn't get a word of that.
Then how come y'asked me in the first place? I told ya you wouldn't understand it!
Sorry. The accent was thicker than I expected.
Well, I'm not doin' <Italic>that</Italic> again.
That was cute. I like it when a girl has an accent.
You're kiddin' me! Y'were staring into space just now!
I was spellbound, that's all.
Aww. Well ain't that sweet of ya to say. I guess I can let my accent slip out around ya every now and then.
Oh! Kiryu-san, tsk tsk.
Y'got a piece of rice stuck on your cheek.
Really? Where?
Here, lemme take it off for ya.
Yes please.
Okay, sit still now, 'kay?
I can do it.
...There.
Ya missed it.
What? Where?
I'm not going to fall for that trick.
Ya do too! Here, on your right cheek!
There, I got it for ya!
You're a little bit of a brat sometimes aren't ya, Kiryu-san?
Sometimes. I'm not always like this.
Would y'rather I not point this sorta thing out from now on?
Don't worry about it. It won't happen again, anyway.
Oh, reeeally?
Don't tell me there's still more.
Hahahaha!
No, please do. I'd rather you point it out.
If I see any, I'll be sure to get it off for ya. Just don't go puttin' a piece of rice on your face on purpose before ya show up, okay?
That wouldn't be so bad.
Hahahaha! That'd be real silly though, havin' a client who came by with rice stuck to his face all the time!
Well, I'll be ready next time!
I won't. It's just a piece of rice. Not like it's a big deal.
Hehe, sorry 'bout that. Guess I kinda got caught in the moment.
Pass me a hand towel. I want to clean my face.
Y'want a towel to wipe your face, Kiryu-san?
How else would I get it off? I want to make sure I don't have any more rice on my face.
Aww, I was just teasin' ya! Besides, despite what people say, it's not actually a big deal to wipe your face with a hand towel.
It isn't?
I mean if someone's got a greasy face, it's loads better for them to wipe it off than to just leave it like that, right?
That reminds me! Can I tell ya somethin'?
There was a customer here earlier who had tonkotsu ramen before coming in!
I did, too. Just before I came here.
Whaaat? Ew, gross! That stuff makes yer breath reek! Keep your head turned while you're talking t'me!
...There sure are a lot of food stalls in this neighborhood.
I know! It sucks!
I like them. Food stalls in other parts of the country don't usually have tonkotsu ramen.
I know it's a local Hakata specialty n' all, but not every food stall's gotta serve it! That stuff stinks somethin' fierce!
What sucks about it?
It reeks, that's what! I gotta practically hold my nose shut when I walk by those darn food stalls!
Did it make you hungry?
No, the exact opposite! It killed my appetite.
'Cause it smells plain awful!
Like, I can deal with someone's breath reekin' of liquor, but tonkotsu just smells the worst!
People need to mind their manners. If someone doesn't pay attention to whether they have bad breath or body odor, then they're just a creepy old man.
I know, right!? I wish all of my clients were like you, Kiryu-san.
But I guess there are certain things you just have to put up with.
Maybe if you ate it you'd learn to like it. Women like the rich taste of tonkotsu, too.
I know, I know! The flavor ain't the issue, it's the smell! After ya eat it, it just lingers forever.
I wish someone would make a tonkotsu ramen that didn't stink so bad.
Why not move then? That way the smell won't bother you anymore.
What!? Y'want me to move over tonkotsu ramen!?
I thought you hated it so much you couldn't stand it.
I can't. Every time I leave my house I get all bummed out 'cause the smell of tonkotsu in the air.
So are you just going to put up with it forever?
Okay, I get ya. I'll think about it! Heck, maybe movin' to Tokyo or Osaka might be nice!
You really hate it that much?
I can deal with someone's breath reekin' of liquor, but tonkotsu smells the absolute worst!
Huh? But didn't ya say that y'just had some tonkotsu ramen a little while ago?
Uh, well, yes. But I at least stay mindful of things like that, so I'm okay.
That so? Well, then from now on, please make it a point to not eat tonkotsu ramen before y'visit the club.
Okay, can do.
So I'm a big fan of shoppin', but lately I haven't been doin' so great at it.
Not doing great how?
Like I keep buyin' too much stuff, and then after I feel wicked guilty.
